definition.simple: When a solid turns directly into a gas, skipping the liquid phase entirely.
definition.academic: The process of transformation directly from the solid phase to the gaseous phase, without passing through an intermediate liquid phase.

examples: Dry ice (solid CO2) turning into fog.

common_misconceptions: All solids turn into liquids before becoming gases. (Correction: Sublimation proves this wrong. Substances like camphor or naphthalene balls skip the liquid state.)
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student to think about naphthalene balls (mothballs) kept in winter clothes. Do they leave a wet puddle behind?
